name: Dart pub hosted registry
auth: Use an access token with repository read/write permissions. pub stores the environment variable name and reads AW_TOKEN at runtime; never put a real token in pubspec.yaml.
fresh_home: Run in a disposable client container with a new /work mount, or a new temporary project directory with all the client home/cache paths below. The acceptance harness uses a new scenario directory and container. Never reuse your normal client home for this check.
prerequisites: A trusted HTTPS endpoint is required for token authentication.
Producer and consumer each have their own pubspec.yaml; producer declares a publish_to URL for the selected repository.

configure.code:
export PUB_CACHE="$(mktemp -d)"
export PUB_HOSTED_URL="$AW_URL/artifactory/api/pub/$AW_REPO"
dart pub token add "$PUB_HOSTED_URL" --env-var AW_TOKEN

name: hello_pub
version: 1.2.3
description: Example package
environment:
  sdk: ^3.10.0
publish_to: "${AW_URL}/artifactory/api/pub/${AW_REPO}"
configure.note: Producer pubspec.yaml: substitute repository variables and include lib/, README.md, CHANGELOG.md and LICENSE.

publish.note: Publish only to the classes listed here. A federated recipe proves one-node behavior; remote repositories are read-only client sources.

install.note: Use the selected repository key. Virtual resolution requires readable configured members; remote resolution requires an administrator-configured upstream.

steps.note: Run from a fresh consumer directory whose pubspec.yaml declares hello_pub: ^1.0.0; PUB_HOSTED_URL selects this registry.

limitations: Do not use an HTTP endpoint or disable certificate checking for production token use.
A fresh PUB_CACHE requires adding the environment token reference again.
